messages.text: just finished cleaning up after dinner. kids are finally winding down 😅
Sounds like you’ve had a busy evening! 😊 How are *you* feeling now that things are settling down—relieved, tired, or maybe both?
a little sad, honestly. like... i smiled through dinner, but it wasn’t real, you know? just automatic.

It sounds like you’ve been putting on a brave face while feeling something quite different inside. That can be exhausting over time. Do you have a sense of what might be underneath that sadness tonight?

it’s just... i do it all the time. with my friends, my family. like today when my friend said i should “just go for a walk and snap out of it.” i nodded and said “yeah, maybe,” but inside i wanted to scream lol.

It can feel really isolating when the people around you don’t fully understand what you’re experiencing. Your reaction makes sense—your feelings are valid, even if others minimize them. Would you like to talk about what “snap out of it” misses for you, or what’s actually going on beneath the surface?
i just hate that i can’t say how i really feel... like, what if it makes them uncomfortable? what if they think i’m ungrateful? i end up swallowing it all. again.

You’re carrying a lot by keeping those feelings inside, and that can be draining. Worrying about others’ comfort often means your own needs get pushed aside. Would it feel safer to first explore those feelings here, where you can speak openly without judgment?
yeah... it’s like i’m scared to be honest. what if they think i’m broken or too much? so i just… disappear a little. every time.

It’s painful when hiding parts of yourself feels like the only way to protect relationships. That “disappearing” can slowly erode your sense of self. Would you like to explore small, low‑risk ways to practice sharing your feelings so you can stay more visible?
i do want to be honest... but i’m also terrified. like, what if they pull away? what if they get tired of me? idk, maybe i’m overthinking.

It’s not overthinking—those fears are very real when vulnerability has felt risky before. Opening up doesn’t have to be all‑or‑nothing; small steps can help you test the waters. What’s one person or situation where you might feel just a little safer to share something genuine?
huh... i just realized something. i don’t even know who i *could* trust. i’ve never actually tried being real with anyone. i just assumed it wouldn’t go well.

That’s an important realization—it shows how much your mind has been protecting you from possible rejection. Sometimes assumptions like that become habits, even without evidence. Would you like to explore what trust might look like for you and how to identify people who feel safer?
is it weird that i want to be seen… but also want to hide? like, part of me wants someone to *get* it, but the other part just wants to stay quiet forever?

That push‑pull is very common when you’ve long protected yourself through hiding. Wanting to be seen and fearing it can coexist, and it often signals a deep need for connection as well as safety. We could look at ways to honor both needs—choosing moments and people where being seen feels less risky.
yeah... it’s like i’ve been so busy protecting everyone else that i forgot i matter too. weird to say that out loud.

It’s not weird—it’s a powerful truth you’ve just voiced. Recognizing that you matter is a big step toward caring for yourself. How would it feel to imagine giving yourself even a little of the compassion you offer others?
actually... kinda nice. like, i don’t have to have answers. just saying it helps.

That’s a beautiful insight—sometimes simply naming what’s true can bring relief. You don’t need to solve everything at once; allowing space for your feelings is already a form of care. Would you like to spend a moment noticing what that “kinda nice” sensation feels like in your body right now?
i don’t know about my body... but maybe i can try something small? like, next time i feel myself fading out... i’ll just pause. not fix it, just... notice.

That’s a gentle and realistic step—pausing creates space to acknowledge what’s happening without pressure to change it. Even brief moments of awareness can start to shift how you relate to yourself. Would you like some ideas for cues or reminders to help you notice when you start fading out?
nah, i don’t wanna overthink it. just... see what happens. maybe it’ll stick, maybe not. no pressure.

That sounds like a healthy, low‑pressure approach—experimenting without judgment. Giving yourself permission to just see what happens can keep it manageable and kind. How are you feeling right now as we wrap up tonight’s conversation?
thanks for listening. it helps... more than i can say.
I’m glad this space has been helpful for you. You’ve shared some important truths tonight, and that takes courage. Take care of yourself as you settle in, and remember you matter too.
